# Shop smart: 7 tips for a safer holiday season


More holiday cheer. Less financial worry.


Great Southern Bank


Good deals. Great gifts. No surprises from scammers.


The holidays are a time for making memories, finding the perfect gifts and enjoying a little extra cheer. Unfortunately, scammers are looking to take advantage of the busy shopping season, too.


At Great Southern Bank, your financial security matters to us. Whether you're shopping online or checking off your list in stores, these seven tips can help you protect your money and enjoy the holidays with greater peace of mind.


## 1. Make sure the deal is the real deal


Unbelievably low prices and limited time offers are common tactics scammers use to create a sense of urgency. Before making a purchase, compare prices across trusted retailers and research unfamiliar sellers. If a deal seems too good to be true, it probably is.


## 2. Think before you click


Scammers can use artificial intelligence (AI) to create convincing advertisements, fraudulent websites and fake customer reviews.


Instead of clicking on links in promotional emails or social media ads, visit the retailer's official website or app directly. Always double-check the web address before entering personal or payment information.


## 3. Choose how you pay wisely


Consider using a credit card when shopping online, as credit cards generally offer additional consumer protections.


Be cautious of unfamiliar sellers who request payment through gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency or peer-to-peer payment apps. These payments funds can be difficult to recover if something goes wrong.


## 4. Watch for fake delivery and order notifications


Expecting a package? Scammers are counting on it.


Fraudulent texts and emails may claim you've missed a delivery, owe a shipping fee or made a purchase you don't recognize. These messages often contain malicious links or fraudulent customer service numbers.


Verify orders and track packages directly through the retailer or shipping company's official website or app.


## 5. Give gift cards with confidence


Gift cards are popular holiday presents, but they're also a common target for fraud.


Purchase gift cards from trusted retailers, inspect packaging for signs of tampering and keep your receipts. Avoid purchasing cards with exposed security codes.


Remember, gift cards are for giving, not for paying unexpected bills or resolving urgent financial requests.


## 6. Keep your personal information personal


Use strong, unique passwords and enable multifactor authentication whenever possible. Avoid making purchases or accessing financial information over unsecured public Wi-Fi.


Never share your banking credentials or one-time security codes in response to an unexpected call, text or email. If someone claims to be your bank, contact your financial institution directly using a trusted phone number.


## 7. Check your list. Check your transactions.


With more purchases happening throughout the holidays, unfamiliar charges can be easier to overlook. Review your account activity regularly and[set up transaction alerts](https://www.greatsouthernbank.com/about/alerts-and-notifications) to stay connected to your money.


If something doesn't look right, don't hesitate to reach out. Contact Great Southern Bank immediately at **800-749-7113** if you notice suspicious activity or believe your financial information has been compromised. Our team is here to help you navigate the next steps.


## Make it a season well spent


The holidays should be filled with good memories, not financial worries. With a little extra awareness and a few smart shopping habits, you can spend the season with greater confidence.


At Great Southern Bank, we're here for you during the holidays and every day in between. Your peace of mind matters to us, and we're committed to keeping you informed.


Explore more fraud prevention tips and resources to stay one step ahead of scammers.
